title: Drug Discovery and Molecular Simulation
answer: Protein structure, new molecules, simulated trials, toxicity forecasting and repurposing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Protein Structure Prediction
children.blurb: Protein structure prediction uses machine learning to estimate the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence.

children.name: Designing New Molecules
children.blurb: Designing new molecules with AI covers computational generation and evaluation of candidate chemical structures for drug discovery, including small molecules, peptides, and biologics.

children.name: Simulated Clinical Trials
children.blurb: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial.

children.name: Toxicity Forecasting
children.blurb: Toxicity forecasting uses machine learning to predict whether a candidate molecule will cause harm in a biological system before it enters costly laboratory or animal testing.

children.name: Drug Repurposing
children.blurb: Drug repurposing is the practice of finding new therapeutic uses for medicines that are already approved or have passed early safety testing.

sections.body: This field uses machine learning to search chemical and biological space. AI now predicts how amino acid chains fold into protein shapes, proposes candidate molecules with desired properties, and estimates how those molecules might behave in the body. It also runs large scale simulations of patient populations to test ideas before physical trials, forecasts which compounds are likely to harm cells or organs, and screens existing approved drugs for new uses. These are working tools in pharmaceutical research, not just academic demonstrations.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The most mature area is protein structure prediction, where models can often produce accurate static shapes for single proteins, though flexible regions, complexes, and the effects of mutations remain harder. Molecule design can generate plausible compounds, but most candidates still fail later in real testing because the models do not capture the full complexity of living systems. Simulated trials and toxicity forecasting are useful for ranking and reducing risk, not for replacing physical evidence, and their predictions can miss rare or long term effects. Drug repurposing has found some real opportunities, but confirmation still requires traditional clinical work. The site tracks 805 scientific models, and this section reflects a field with strong narrow successes and clear limits.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI predicts a protein's shape would start with Protein Structure Prediction, which explains the core methods and what they can and cannot resolve. Designing New Molecules covers the generative side, where models propose new chemical structures, and it connects naturally to Toxicity Forecasting, which asks whether those structures are likely to be safe. Simulated Clinical Trials sits between the lab and the clinic, showing how AI tries to model patient responses before a real study begins. Drug Repurposing takes a different route, using existing drugs and known safety data to search for new indications, and it often draws on the same molecular and protein tools described in the other pages. Together the five pages move from the shape of a single protein to the behavior of a molecule in a population.
